episode_title: Fire the Chef: How Systems Save Your Client Experience| EPISODE 238

real_qa.q: What percentage of clients do professional service businesses retain annually according to industry benchmarks?
real_qa.r: Industry benchmarks suggest that professional service businesses retain about 84% of clients each year. This means that even strong businesses will lose clients, which is normal and part of business.
real_qa.requete: professional services client retention rate benchmark

real_qa.q: Why did Francesca Moy's three former clients return to AEVS after working with other agencies?
real_qa.r: The three former clients returned to AEVS because they realized they were oversold on a cheaper solution that lacked proper support. The other provider couldn't replace the experience AEVS provided: fast communication, dedicated client service managers, staff training, mentorship, and consistent support. They felt supported within the AEVS journey rather than left alone on their own devices.
real_qa.requete: why clients return to AEVS after leaving

real_qa.q: What does 'fire the chef' mean as a business system principle according to Francesca Moy?
real_qa.r: The principle means that a business should find a great chef or expert, document their recipe or process, then remove dependency on that individual by creating a standardized system everyone can follow. This ensures consistency regardless of which team member delivers the service or how they feel that day. Francesca implemented this at AEVS, resulting in five-star experiences for all clients regardless of team member personality or mood.
real_qa.requete: fire the chef business systems principle

real_qa.q: How do systems improve client experience beyond efficiency and automation?
real_qa.r: Systems create consistency and enable strong service delivery every time. They solve problems faster, support team performance, and give clients confidence by setting clear expectations. Systems protect the client experience by ensuring the same level of service regardless of which team member delivers it or their circumstances on any given day.
real_qa.requete: how systems improve client experience consistency

real_qa.q: What is the key difference between clients valuing a product versus valuing the experience after delivery?
real_qa.r: Most business owners improve their products but neglect the experience they deliver. Clients don't necessarily value the product or service itself—they value what happens after delivery and whether they feel supported. Francesca discovered that her returning clients valued the post-delivery support, communication, and feeling of being looked after more than the core service itself.
real_qa.requete: client value product versus experience after delivery

guest.bio_context: Francesca Moy is the founder of AEVS, a service-based business that has grown to over 100k per month. She hosts the Business Behind the Scenes podcast and runs the Successful Entrepreneur Lounge Facebook group with over 11,000 members. She has built her business around systems and client experience, learning from three former clients who returned after working with competitors.
